ambiguities.text: Individual entries must fit within 512-byte UDP DNS limits - behavior for larger entries not specified
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume entries exceeding 512 bytes should be rejected as invalid. Publishers must ensure all entries fit within this limit.

ambiguities.text: The specification does not define caching behavior or TTL for DNS records
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume clients should respect standard DNS TTL values but may refresh more frequently for security-critical updates.

ambiguities.text: How often should clients re-check for updates is not specified
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume clients should periodically check (e.g., every hour) and compare sequence numbers to detect updates.

implicit_assumptions.description: The DNS list publisher is assumed to be a trusted party that maintains accurate and up-to-date node lists
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Malicious publisher could perform eclipse attacks by only publishing nodes they control

implicit_assumptions.description: DNS infrastructure is available and returns correct records (modulo signature verification)
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: DNS unavailability would prevent node discovery; corrupted responses are detected by hash verification

implicit_assumptions.description: Attackers cannot forge signatures matching the publisher's secp256k1 public key
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Attackers could inject malicious node lists, enabling eclipse attacks

implicit_assumptions.description: Clients use multiple independent DNS sources to prevent single-source eclipse attacks
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Single compromised or malicious DNS source could eclipse clients relying solely on it
